clue.text: Rate at which storm arrives?

parts.note: a storm comes with flashes of lightning, so its arrival speed is jokingly the idiom for something extremely fast

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster wonders how quickly the coming storm will hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for great rapidity is read literally as the pace of the storm's bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes extreme velocity, here taken as the literal pace of a thunderstorm's flashes.

clue.text: Drop round

definitions.meaning: a small round body or sphere, as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: A bead of liquid is a tiny drop, and it is also a small spherical mass.

clue.text: Grotty kennel housing dog

indicators.note: the words Grotty kennel are said to house the answer, which sits inside them across the gap

explanation.surface: A shabby kennel is home to a mutt.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel or cur is called this in British and Yorkshire usage.

clue.text: Get together during ninth period?

parts.note: during means in, as in 'in the night'
a term is a period of time, as a school term
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A suggestion to meet up in the ninth lesson of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To blend things with one another is to bring them together into a mixture.

clue.text: Dark blue

definitions.meaning: dark as in dim and unlit
blue as in sad and depressed

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both a dimly lit place and a despondent mood.

clue.text: Journey's formidable, stopping heartless plunder

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the formidable word is put inside the other
heartless means the central letter of the word for plunder is removed

parts.note: to pillage is to plunder
grim means forbidding or formidable

explanation.surface: A trek is daunting when it interrupts a looting spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle L, leaving PILAGE; 'stopping' puts GRIM into it. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a religious trip to a shrine or sacred place.

clue.text: Prophet finding canal after second half of freeze

indicators.note: after places the canal name behind the letters taken from freeze
second half of says to take the last three of the six letters of freeze

parts.note: the Kiel Canal links the North Sea and the Baltic in Germany

explanation.surface: A seer discovers a waterway once the frost is half over.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezekiel is an Old Testament prophet with a book of the Bible named after him.

clue.text: A certain solver will not use it

definitions.text: A certain solver will not use it

parts.words: A certain solver will not use it
parts.note: a solver sure of the answers writes in ink without needing to rub anything out, so needs no eraser

explanation.surface: A confident crossword solver scorns some aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'certain' means sure of oneself, not 'a particular'; such a solver never needs to erase.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the British name for an eraser, used to rub out pencil mistakes.

clue.text: Prepare to fire at ducks or another bird

parts.note: to cock a gun is to make it ready to fire
a duck is a zero in cricket, so two ducks are OO

explanation.surface: A hunter readies his gun to shoot at ducks or some other fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatoo is a crested parrot, a bird other than the ducks of the surface.

clue.text: Right across island, rest until late?

indicators.note: across says the right lies over the island, enclosing it

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone crosses an island on the right and then sleeps late.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed past the usual hour in the morning is a common British idiom for a lazy start.

clue.text: Pair well-directed in rhyme

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme the boy and girl went up the hill to fetch a pail of water, so they were directed to a well

explanation.surface: A couple steered skilfully in some verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-directed' seems to mean skilfully guided, but it means sent toward a well.
explanation.definitionFit: The two children of the nursery rhyme were sent up a hill for water.

clue.text: Water? A quart? Not right!

indicators.note: Not says the abbreviation for right is to be missing from the quart

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether a quart of water is the right measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is the Latin word for water, used in English in compounds and labels.

clue.text: Thirsty, swallow single drink

parts.note: dry means thirsty
the martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is one, a single

explanation.surface: Parched, someone gulps down one drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like a verb for drinking but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cocktail of gin with a little vermouth, a classic alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Light bothered playmates, including female

indicators.note: including says the rearranged playmates take in the female letter
bothered suggests being stirred up, so the letters of playmates are rearranged

explanation.surface: Annoyed playmates, a girl among them, cause a glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered' gives SAETYLAMP from PLAYMATES; 'including' puts F into it.
explanation.definitionFit: The miner's lamp designed not to ignite firedamp is a kind of lamp, hence a light.

clue.text: Continue to look after a bird

parts.note: to keep is to look after or maintain
the tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone is told to carry on caring for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to persist doggedly with an activity rather than give up.

clue.text: One walker or another failing to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the first letter of the other walker is dropped

parts.note: a rambler is another kind of walker, one who hikes in the countryside

explanation.surface: One hiker, or a second whose start falls short.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who strolls at a leisurely pace is a walker.

clue.text: Team's method included to left or right

indicators.note: included says the method is placed within the team's letters

parts.note: a side is a team, so team's gives side plus the S
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A team's tactics take in moving the ball laterally.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving laterally means going toward one flank or the other rather than ahead.

clue.text: Steal and occasionally deal in coin

parts.note: nick is British slang for steal

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of deal is taken

explanation.surface: Pilfer and sometimes trade in money.
explanation.definitionFit: The American five-cent piece is named after the metal it was made from.

clue.text: Unit of heat, one of many counted by weight-watcher

definitions.meaning: the unit of heat energy in physics

definitions.text: one of many counted by weight-watcher
definitions.meaning: dieters count the energy content of food in these units

explanation.definitionFit: The same energy measure appears in physics and on food labels read by dieters.

clue.text: Grab Nick, staggering to get nipper

indicators.note: staggering suggests lurching about, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Seizing a reeling Nick to collar a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' looks like British slang for a child but means something that nips with claws.
explanation.definitionFit: This large crustacean pinches with its claws, so it is literally a nipper.

clue.text: Supposed to have place in plant

indicators.note: in says the word for place sits inside the plant

parts.note: a reed is a water plant
to put is to place

explanation.surface: Someone is meant to have a spot in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something generally believed or assumed to be so is said to be thus regarded.

clue.text: Direct control

definitions.meaning: to control or rule a country or body

explanation.definitionFit: To rule or steer a state or organisation means both directing it and controlling it.

clue.text: Encourage rascal to get rid of posh Republican flag

parts.note: to jolly someone along is to encourage them

indicators.note: to get rid of says the posh letter is removed from the rascal

parts.note: a rogue is a rascal
U means upper-class, posh, in British usage

explanation.surface: Urging a scoundrel to dump a smart Republican banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones banner flown by pirate ships is a flag.

clue.text: Feature of, perhaps, each church

indicators.note: Feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A part, possibly, of every church building.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and hidden word together also read as a description of the answer: an apse is a feature of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition stands for a church by the recess at its east end; an apse is a part of one.

clue.text: Beast turned up with mother

indicators.note: turned means the little word up is read backwards

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An animal arrived with its mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads as 'arrived', but 'turned' reverses UP.
explanation.definitionFit: The cougar or mountain lion is a big cat, a wild beast.

clue.text: Uncovered gravlax stirred to provide grub

indicators.note: stirred suggests mixing, so the remaining letters are rearranged
uncovered means the outer letters are stripped off, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: Cured salmon unwrapped and mixed to serve as food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' leaves RAVLA from gravlax; 'stirred' rearranges it. 'grub' seems to mean food but is the insect sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the immature wormlike stage of an insect.

clue.text: Ascertain amount of cooked veal before you, we hear, prepared tea

indicators.note: before places the cooked veal ahead of the next piece
cooked suggests the meat is reworked, so its letters are rearranged
we hear says the word is said aloud and entered as a letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word you is said aloud

indicators.note: prepared suggests the drink is made up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook gauges how much veal was made before serving you tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns VEAL into EVAL, 'we hear' gives U for 'you', and 'prepared' turns TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess or appraise is to work out the value or extent of something.

clue.text: What to do with glove in cold weather to retain skill

definitions.text: What to do with glove in cold weather
definitions.meaning: literally, one keeps a hand inside the glove for warmth
the idiom means to practise enough to stay proficient

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for staying in practice is read literally as keeping fingers warm inside a mitten.
